title: Astrid and the Glasshouse
premise: Coral Vane has spent seven years writing postcards to a burned-down glasshouse address, mailing letters to a family that no longer exists and a sister who may not have survived the fire. At his mother's funeral, a stranger named Astrid recognizes the Vane name—one Coral buried along with everything else—and her presence forces him back to the coastal town he fled, where the family house is days from being sold. As Astrid's own connection to the fire unravels, Coral must decide whether to let the sale erase the past or finally claim the truth: that he set the fire, that his sister lived, and that survival cost him the right to be known. He ends the story signing his real name to a letter, mailed to a new address where his sister actually answers.
about_author: Noor Ashgrove is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing unclaimed letters in a provincial records office. Astrid and the Glasshouse is her second novel, written in a rented cottage within sight of the sea.

chapters.title: Poste Restante
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. We meet Coral in his small city flat, a man who writes weekly postcards to an address that burned down years ago, working a job he describes as 'standing in for someone.' His mother's death summons him home. Emotional beat: the numb discipline of a man performing a life he doesn't own.

chapters.title: The Stranger at the Grave
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. At the funeral, a woman named Astrid approaches, calling the family by their old name—Vane-Hollis—a name Coral hasn't heard since the fire. She claims to have known his sister. He lies smoothly and walks away, but his hands shake. Emotional beat: the first crack in seven years of careful invisibility.

chapters.title: Inventory
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral returns to the coastal town to prepare the house for sale, cataloguing rooms that are time capsules: his sister Wren's drawings, his mother's unopened mail. He finds a postcard of his own, returned undeliverable, marked with a forwarding address. Emotional beat: grief arriving late, in the form of objects.

chapters.title: What Astrid Kept
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid, a restorer of damaged photographs, reveals she was Wren's friend before the fire and has kept a box of Wren's letters—letters that contradict Coral's version of events. She came to the funeral deliberately. Emotional beat: Astrid's own quiet grief and her suspicion that Coral is hiding something essential.

chapters.title: The Glasshouse
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral visits the ruins of the glasshouse where the family once grew rare orchids—the fire's origin point. Memory floods back: the night of the blaze, his father's debts, Wren's scream. He tells Astrid nothing. Emotional beat: the past pressing through the floorboards of the present.

chapters.title: Buyer's Agent
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The house sale accelerates; a developer wants the land. Astrid confronts Coral, showing him one of Wren's letters that mentions 'Coral's mistake'—proof Wren knew something about the fire. Coral denies it coldly, and Astrid realizes he isn't lying to her; he's lying to himself. Emotional beat: rising tension, alliance fracturing.

chapters.title: The Undelivered Year
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, in flashback. The full truth surfaces: Coral, seventeen, burned the glasshouse for the insurance money to save the family, believing Wren was away. She wasn't. She survived but was disfigured, and chose to disappear rather than be seen—leaving Coral to carry the guilt alone while their mother chose denial. Emotional beat: devastating clarity about the price of survival.

chapters.title: Sale Day
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The closing approaches. Astrid finds Wren—alive, working at a coastal nursery under another name—and tells her Coral never stopped writing. Wren's rage and longing collide. Meanwhile the developer's surveyors arrive at the house. Emotional beat: hope and betrayal in the same breath; the clock running out.

chapters.title: Ash and Orchid
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Climax. On the morning of the sale, Wren appears at the house. The siblings confront each other among the empty rooms—her fury at being pitied, his confession that the fire was his doing. She reveals she never blamed him; she blamed his silence. The sale proceeds anyway, and Coral lets it, choosing truth over property. Emotional beat: rupture, then the first real breath.

chapters.title: A New Address
chapters.summary: Alternating Coral and Astrid POV, closing with Coral. Months later: the glasshouse land becomes a public garden; Astrid and Coral, tentatively together, restore old photographs of the family. Coral writes a final postcard—not to a ghost, but to Wren, at her real address, signed with his full name. She writes back. Emotional beat: quiet, earned resolution—memory honored, duty released, love begun.
